precepts.text: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house. The way you set it up, the way you do things, that is your beauty. And for you brothers whose wives only clean for presentation when company comes: you have to order your house and demand what the desire of your home is.
precepts.point: Be honest, sisters: when it comes to the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do what you want with the drapes, the pots, the design. Most men are not fighting you over the couch set. So stop acting like submission is slavery; most of that is exaggeration.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” The way she sets it up and the way she does things: that is her beauty.

Ephesians 5 says “as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Submitting “as unto the Lord” means listening to your husband as you would to Christ, and assisting him in what he wants. It is the house of the husband, the house of Abiel, not the house of Abiel and his wife. When you understand whose house it is, you understand whose desires set what the house is supposed to be. If he wants a sound home, give him a sound home; if he wants a clean house, give him a clean house. The confusion comes when a sister thinks her aspirations supersede his. We are on the same team, but somebody is the CEO of the team making the decisions for the franchise.

Be honest, sisters: in the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do pretty much what you want. I don’t give a damn about them pots. The drapes, the knives and forks, the couch set: most men are not tripping over that. As long as he comes home to good food and a clean house, however she got there is fine. So stop acting like submission is straight slavery; most of that is exaggeration. If she wants to lift the carpet and vacuum the cushion every morning, that is her ordering, and that is her beauty.

For the brothers whose wives do not want to clean except when company comes over, cleaning for presentation: you have to order your house. Tell her this is not the desire of your home, this is what needs to be done, and demand it. For the brothers with neat freaks, that is a blessing; sometimes you have to calm them down.

This is also what Titus 2 means by “keepers at home”: a good wife in the ordering of her house, not idle, not a busybody in everybody else’s house, taking care of home.

precepts.text: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church.
precepts.point: If we want to strengthen our families: one, husbands be in order, wife be in order, children, they will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior, and in turn they're putting on the whole armor of God.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'

precepts.why:
“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

The whole armour of God is not put on in pieces. If we want to strengthen our families: one, the husband in order; the wife in order; and the children will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior. The husband is the head as Christ is the head, and the wife submits as unto the Lord.

If the husband and wife are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order. So the order of the house, the husband as head and the wife submitting, is part of the armour that lets the family “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

This is another piece of the whole armour. If you are not redeeming the time because the days are evil, you are not going to teach your children to learn how to fear God. Walking circumspectly, not as fools but as wise, is how a parent sets the example the children follow.

The days are evil: the social media zaps our young out, and Esau sets it up so they can be taken for sweat equity. Redeeming the time means using it for the Lord and for teaching the house, so the family can put on the whole armour of God and “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

The world molds them with its music and its social media; the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs mold them with the law. That repetition in the house is part of putting on the whole armour of God, so they can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

precepts.text: A brother answered what the living water is: that he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word. The living water is the word of God, the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Christ told her, “If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” What is the living water? A brother answered from Ephesians: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

You are cleansed by the washing of water by the word, so the living water is the word of God. What Christ would have given her was understanding: the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together again.

She said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? That shows she understood she was part of the twelve tribes of Israel; she just knew the Jews had no dealings with them. And Christ answered, “Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst”. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they had been disconnected from it for so long.

precepts.point: And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; and shall thrust him through when he prophesieth. precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.” What is the fountain? Paul shows it: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. The water is the word. The fountain opened to the nation of Israel is the Bible, the laws of the Most High.

In that day the laws of God will be opened up to the twelve tribes of Israel, with Christ there. It is for sin and for uncleanness: the lies, the wickedness and the evil will be opened up to be judged.

That day is in the wilderness, right before we get to our kingdom. It parallels Ezekiel, where the Lord pleads with us face to face and says, I will cause you to pass under the rod: the rod of correction. Christ will cause all of us, sons and daughters, mothers and fathers, to pass under that rod, washed by the word. If we have not learned to keep God's laws by then, that is the day of judgment.

That is why the names of the idols are cut off and no more remembered. When the Lord smites down the one teaching lies, everybody instantly drops what he taught; nobody talks about it anymore. The fountain of the word cleanses the nation, and everything that is not in line with this Bible is put to death with the ones that taught it.

precepts.point: Hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen. Fear not: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty. Thirsty for what? For the truth.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Jacob, “Fear not”, and promises, “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty.” Thirsty for what? Thirsty for the truth. Paul shows what that water is: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” The water represents the word of God.

Read Isaiah with that in mind. “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”: I will pour the word of God upon them that are thirsty for the truth. “and floods upon the dry ground”: the floods also represent the word of God, poured out on the dry ground, these places wherein we dwell. “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring”: his spirit upon his people and his blessing upon their children.

God only chose Israel, and this washing is for his chosen, Jacob and Jesurun, “whom I have chosen.” The Lord made us and formed us from the womb, and he will help us.

When the word is poured out, “they shall spring up as among the grass.” That is what we are looking at now: the Israelites are waking up and springing up worldwide like grass. And verse 5 shows three kinds of Israelites waking up: one says “I am the Lord’s”, acknowledging we are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; another takes on a new name and calls himself “by the name of Jacob”; another changes his surname and will “surname himself by the name of Israel.” It is the word of God, the water, that cleanses them and brings them back.

precepts.point: The head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. Paul is not making anything up or creating a list; he went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Paul is not making anything up. He is not creating a list and saying, I'll place this person here and that person there. He went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning, when Adam named his wife Eve, and he does it in other places too.

Ephesians says it again: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Is there any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church.

So the order runs: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or out of their position, what are they? The damn devil. That goes for the men too: men who step out of their role and want to be a mama's boy, you are the damn devil. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

There cannot be a commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle with something, and we know the fight, but never be the one who says, I can get with everything else but that right there I just can't do; he's an idiot, I can't follow him. That is not what the scripture said.

There are going to be sisters who find out they are not going to get the kingdom because they did not respect nor reverence their husband. Some sisters said, damn, so we're going to go to hell because we're disrespectful? Yes. You didn't realize that?

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?” They are going to have the audacity: Lord, I taught classes, I was out in the streets handing out flyers, I didn't eat pork, I left the shrimp alone, I wore fringes every day. “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

What could keep them from knowing the Lord? Iniquity: sin. Sister, every command your husband gives you is law. It is like getting orders from God for you. As long as your husband is not asking you to sin, if he asks you to do something, it is sin if you don't do it.

In the westernized mindset that doesn't compute: he has that much power? You malfunction because you don't believe he is a god; you don't see the Christ in him. You had better read your Bible. He absolutely has that much authority over you, and all the wonderful works in the world will not cover the iniquity of disrespecting him.

Provide means her food, her raiment, her clothing. Lord, I didn't eat pork, I didn't eat shrimp or lobster, I stopped dealing with the prostitutes, I kept the Sabbath day holy. But you didn't take care of your wife or your kids. You were a deadbeat; you did nothing for her; you left the house, living among everybody else doing what you wanted, saying, I'm not dealing with that woman no more. That was your wife. That man has denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. Is that man going to see the kingdom? No.

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church”. Is that an option? If I don't do that, will I see the kingdom? The natural thing for the evil man on this side of the earth is to be promiscuous, to roam, with nothing holding him down. Is that love? No.

So what makes you think it's any different when a wife doesn't submit? Your level of faith is shown by the level of respect you have for your husband, because that is the level of respect you have for God. The same goes for the man: the way you love and care for your wife is the level of love you have for Christ. If you don't love, protect and provide for her, you're an infidel; if you don't respect your husband and do what he says, you're an infidel. Fringes and every Sabbath don't matter.

Nobody says, I won't eat pork unless; I'll keep the Sabbath day if. No.

Your whole duty in life: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” There is no excuse for not observing a commandment.

You show him through your chaste conversation and your actions that you are going to serve the Lord no matter what; you heap hot coals on his head.

Disrespect should never be an option. Only Satan gives you that option. If submission depends on his behavior, it isn't submission; it's manipulation. God told you to submit without a caveat, because it is a commandment, and keeping the commandments is the whole duty.

Brothers here have destabilized whole households playing around with a business because the wife makes good money, taking more risk with more lives on the line than they ever took alone.

precepts.why:
Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and showing honour in the household to the wife and the children. Exodus 21:10 shows the provision: “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”. He has to provide for his wife's basic needs. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”. That is how bad the Lord sees it.

Ephesians 5 describes the husband's role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body”. And verse 25: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”. He gave himself for it. It is a sacrificial relationship.

That is why the brother who destabilizes the whole household economically is out of order. Hard times may come and the wife may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took woman's work to support the house. But Tobit did not say, you're doing good, so I'm going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers here have done that: not happy with the job, so try this business, since the wife makes good money. Knowing damn well you couldn't take those risks by yourself, you take more risk with more lives on the line than when you were responsible only for you.

The husband's measure of accountability is the heavier one. He is the saviour of the body: accountable for his wife, the house, the children, and for those moving for the nation, the nation behind that too. He puts his soul on the line for that accountability, and that is what giving himself for it means.

precepts.text: If thou marry, thou hast not sinned, nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh. There will be trouble; how you handle it depends on the expectations you went in with.
precepts.point: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord: the same way you submit to Christ and the Most High, not less and not below it. Scripture defines marriage by function, not feelings. Traditions carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. Function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Paul says plainly: “But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh.” Marriage is no sin, but there will be trouble in it. Every marriage meets conflict.

How a couple deals with that trouble depends on the expectations they carried into it. Scripture does not define marriage by feelings; it defines it by function. Marriage originated with God. Culture later added the ceremonies, made it a business, and put unrealistic expectations on it. The traditions may carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. That is the modern confusion: putting feelings in front of function.

So the trouble in the flesh is expected, and it is met with the order of Ephesians 5: the husband as the head who gives himself for the wife, the wife submitting “as unto the Lord.” Marriage is meant to function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

precepts.text: A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace. The Bible calls for peace in the marriage, not strife, variance, or division. Peace, not passion; the wife rejoices her husband through reverence and he walks in his integrity.
precepts.point: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord: the same way you submit to Christ and the Most High, not less and not below it. Scripture defines marriage by function, not feelings. Traditions carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. Function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.” The Bible calls for peace in the marriage: not war, not strife, not enmity, not division, not variance.

This is how the trouble in the flesh of 1 Corinthians 7:28 is handled. The wife focuses on rejoicing her husband through reverence, and then he stands in his integrity, because there is peace in the household. Peace, not passion. Peace, not feelings.

That reverence is what Ephesians 5:33 asks: “the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Reverence is beyond respect. It is a profound, heartfelt attitude of awe, that manifests as obedience and submission. It cannot be done as a job description; it has to come from the heart, and if a sister does not have that spirit she has to pray for it. When it comes from genuine respect and a desire to please the Lord, she will not be derelict in her duties, and the house has peace.

precepts.text: Keep the ordinances as I delivered them to you: the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. Grounded in that order, love becomes stronger, joy and passion follow, and the marriage becomes more durable over time.
precepts.point: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord: the same way you submit to Christ and the Most High, not less and not below it. Scripture defines marriage by function, not feelings. Traditions carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. Function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Paul praises the brethren that they “keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.” Then he gives the summary of the order: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.”

This is the same order as Ephesians 5:23: “the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” The woman’s list of duties may look longer, but the man’s responsibilities carry much more weight, because he is the one that is accountable. A sister’s accountability is for herself; the husband is accountable for her, the house, the children and the nation. He is the saviour of the body. Does that not deserve honour?

When marriage is grounded in the order God established, love becomes stronger. The passion and the joy come, not romance, which is a new modern term, but the more meaningful feelings behind it, and the marriage becomes more durable over time. Marriage mirrors Christ and the Israelites, and prophecy is not entertainment: it is a sign for us to correct ourselves and get things in order, individually and as a people.

precepts.text: Walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, alienated from the life of God through the blindness of their heart, given over unto lasciviousness. But ye have not so learned Christ.
precepts.point: Be ye followers of God as dear children, and walk in love. But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints. Paul wrote this way because that is what the Ephesians used to be caught up in.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; And walk in love”. “But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints”. Why did Paul write to the Ephesians that way? Because that is what they used to be caught up in. Ephesus was a tough pagan environment. The worship of Diana, Artemis, involved all manner of lewd behaviour: they filled the great theatre, they had orgies, they got drunk, witchcraft, idolatry. Diana is the queen of heaven, the same as Ashtaroth, and the same as the Yoruba goddess, and our people were caught up in it in ancient times and today.

Chapter 4 shows it: “This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart”.

“Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness. But ye have not so learned Christ”. Paul wrote in that form because he knew the lifestyle they came from, living as the Gentiles.

They were once “Gentiles in the flesh” and “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”, but now made nigh by the blood of Christ, “fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”: the northern kingdom, the so-called Argentinians, Colombians, Brazilians, Venezuelans, Puerto Ricans and Mexicans, the Israelites according to the Bible. So our people need to wake up and repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and flee from idolatry, or receive the same judgment coming on America.

precepts.text: Walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.
precepts.point: Christ gave himself an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour, and we are to walk in love and become the same sacrifice for our brothers and sisters. When they put you to death out here, the Lord sees it as a sacrifice on the altar; that is what the altar in Babylon represents.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.” Christ gave himself as a sacrifice for us. His blood on the altar is the atonement Leviticus speaks of: “I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls”.

Likewise, we are going to have to do the same thing for our brothers and our sisters. We have to become their sacrifice. Many don't pay attention to this: when they put you to death out here, the Lord looks at it as a sacrifice. That is why it is said that in Babylon they see your altar. What did they do on the altar? Offer blood sacrifice. They are going to put us to death out here, and that is what the altar represents.

We are unto God “a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish”. The ones who walk the other way are the ones who “in time past” walked “according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. Those children of disobedience are in the churches, in the mosques, in everything, thinking that is the way. Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. The way is through God's law, statutes and commandments, to his son Jesus the Christ.

So walking in love is walking as Christ walked: keeping the commandments, and giving ourselves for our people as he gave himself, an offering the Lord receives as a sweetsmelling savour.

precepts.text: The husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church.
precepts.point: The husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the church. There is no glory for the women unless the men have theirs.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
The apostles asked, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” That is what we want, brothers, and you sisters should want it too. But it is not going to be returned unless the man is in his proper order. The Most High is not going to give the kingdom to the women and not the men; there is no glory for the sisters unless the men get their glory as prophesied.

Some sisters make a face at that and say, I love Jesus directly. So Paul backs it up: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” It is the same thing: there is no salvation except through Christ, and the man is the saviour of the body. The flock of the pasture is men, and the saviours on Mount Zion are men.

Look at the so-called white woman, whom the other women worship, with the Vogue magazines and Miss America. She would have none of that if she did not support her man; the man had to guarantee her sovereignty and her safety so she could prance around. Those women were behind their men a thousand percent, even in evil, going out to the lynchings to support them. Yet that same man keeps his woman in check and tells our women they don't need you brothers. All women expect their men to guarantee their protection; the fact that this must even be addressed among our women is evidence of our destruction.

The charger only has a need because the phone was created. The woman is the charging station, but with no phone you aren't charging nothing. The charger came out of the phone: woman was taken out of man, and she is a helpmate and a comfort to him so he can guarantee her protection and the offspring. You won't get past this brother, because you came from the brother. So the charging stations need to be in full force, and the men have to get in order so the kingdom can be restored.

precepts.text: Let every one of you so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.
precepts.point: Reverence is deep respect laced with awe; its opposite is contempt.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” This is your wisdom, sisters: honor the husband. Dishonoring him in pride sounds like, damn, I got to be up under a man? Nah, I got a direct line to Jesus. And “an honest woman will reverence her husband.”

Look up reverence and meditate on it; it goes beyond respect. It is a feeling or attitude of deep respect tinged with awe, veneration. Your man is on a pedestal; he walks in the house and everything gets still to welcome him home. Women understand it, because they do it when they go to work. And there is an outward manifestation: actions that demonstrate it, not, you know I had a hard day, you know what my boss said. If the definition is hard, read the opposite and don’t do that: contempt. If there is a tinge of contempt in your spirit toward your husband, that is what Sirach calls ungodly. We have seen marriages in the congregation where the wife showed nothing but contempt.

Paul uses the same word: “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” The husband gives first. He loves his wife as himself; she is his comfort, she charges his batteries, and he will put his life on the line for her. When you love your wife, your family and your nation, you will go to war to protect it. Any man who lets somebody run over his family is a damn fool.

And the wife reverences her husband. This is how we lost that honor and reverence: the kingdom of heaven suffered violence, and our women were taken from us. The Willie Lynch letter said to break the female until she submits completely to the slaveholder’s will, with no glimmer of honor left for her husband, so she would train her children to labor. That is why we see so much contempt now. Returning our kingdom to order means the husband loving as Christ loved and the wife reverencing her husband again.

precepts.text: That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.
precepts.point: Every man should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour, and wash his wife with the water of the word.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
This is where the man presents his wife to himself, the way Christ does the church: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing”. The honour given to the weaker vessel is the husband washing her with the word, cleansing and sanctifying her until she is without spot.

So you can't do like Adam and say it's the woman you gave me. You had choices. There were proving processes that should have been done properly and correctly, with the right time constraints, before she became yours. And once she is yours, there is no divorce in that. You are in it.

We can either be happy and function the way the Lord says we should function, or the man will give you the version of himself that he needs to survive. David never touched Michal again; he did not divorce her, but that was it, it dried up. A man can tolerate that much longer than a woman can. We should not be bitter and we should not hold one another in contempt. We have to build that thing up.

precepts.text: Sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.
precepts.point: Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double minded.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
God “resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.” The humble submit to God and resist the devil, and James goes on: “Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” How do we purify our minds? Paul shows how Christ cleanses his people: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.”

In Christianity many think that because they dipped themselves in water they are a whole other person. But the true baptism is washing yourself with the word. Sitting here in the class, hearing the scriptures, is that washing. And to sanctify and cleanse by the washing of water by the word means you have to keep the commandments. That is the way you cleanse yourself.

The hands are cleansed of your evil works and evil ways, and the heart is purified of the old worldly mindset. The double minded are the brothers who want to be here but do not want to be here, one foot in and one foot out the door. That is lukewarm, and the Lord will spew the lukewarm out, which means he will put you to death. So either you are hot and kill that old man with the word, or you are lukewarm and you will be killed. Either way, somebody has to die.

The humble who receive that grace are the ones taking steps to kill the old man, sharpening their swords with the word to subdue the evil spirit that plagued them for years before they knew this glorious gospel. That washing is how the Lord draws nigh to them.

precepts.text: Awake, arise from the dead, and walk circumspectly as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
precepts.point: Then walk circumspectly, not as fools but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

note.label: Matthew 25:1-12 | Excerpt from 'The Negro Bible: The Making Of A Slave'

precepts.text: The washing of water by the word: so in order to be born again, it starts in your mind, black man. Your mind must be washed with the word of God.
precepts.point: What does it mean, except a man be born of water and of the Spirit? The ignorant pastor thinks being born again of water means dip him in some water. No, that ain't what it's talking about.

note.label: Message to the Black Man

precepts.text: Christ gave himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour; he is the sacrifice once for all.
precepts.point: In our captivity, with no Levitical priesthood and no temple, keeping the commandments is the offering and the reasonable service: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and we present our bodies a living sacrifice, sacrificing the lusts and pleasures of the flesh to follow the footsteps of Christ. And Ezekiel 20 shows that when Israel is brought back through the wilderness, offerings will be required again in the holy mountain.

note.label: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings

precepts.why:
The burnt sacrifice is “an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord.” That is the language Paul uses of Christ: “And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.”

Christ walked in love and gave himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour. He fulfilled and replaced all these offerings, the bullock killed before the Lord, the blood sprinkled round about upon the altar, the parts laid in order upon the wood, once and for all, in his death and resurrection. He is the sacrifice once for all.

precepts.text: Christ gave himself for the church, to present it a glorious church, holy and without blemish, as the Levitical sacrifices figured.
precepts.point: That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
Christ “loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. The sacrifice without blemish was given so the church could be made without blemish.

“That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.” The same words the law uses of the offering, without blemish, are used of the church Christ presents to himself. That is what the Levitical sacrifices figured.

precepts.text: Sanctified and cleansed with the washing of water by the word; the water is the word.
precepts.point: His seed shall be in many waters means Israel scattered all over the earth, and his kingdom shall be exalted higher than Agag.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters.” The water is the word. Christ loved the church “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.”

The washing of water by the word is how the church is sanctified and cleansed, and that is how you cleanse your spirit. The water poured out of his buckets is the word, and his seed in many waters is Israel scattered all over the earth, with his kingdom exalted higher than Agag.

precepts.text: The husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church; therefore let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.
precepts.point: This is the order of the house: the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church, and he is the saviour of the body; so let the wives be subject to their own husbands in every thing, even in what is vowed in prayer.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
If a wife vowed in her husband’s house and “her husband heard it, and held his peace at her, and disallowed her not: then all her vows shall stand.” Holding his peace is confirming it. “Every vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish it, or her husband may make it void.” But if he holds his peace day after day and then comes later to void it, “then he shall bear her iniquity”: he had the power to stop it and did not. And this runs one way; a wife cannot disallow or nullify her husband’s vow.

That is the order of the house. “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” In every thing, even in what is vowed in prayer. The husband’s power over his wife’s vow is the headship of Christ over the church, set in the house.

precepts.text: Let every one so love his wife even as himself, and the wife see that she reverence her husband; that reverence goes into the honor of feeding the man first, just as the widow did.
precepts.point: The instruction to feed the man of God first is a precept: the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” That reverence goes into the honor of feeding the man first, just as the widow did.

The widow of Zarephath had only “an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse”, and was gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son, “that we may eat it, and die.” Elijah told her, “make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.” The man of God eats first. That is a precept.

She trusted and obeyed, “and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail”. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained.

So sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

precepts.text: He sanctifies and cleanses it with the washing of water by the word; the water here represents the word.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
The waters are the word. Christ sanctifies and cleanses the church “with the washing of water by the word”. The water here represents the word of the Most High.

So the “waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward” are the word issuing out of the spiritual house, the house of Israel. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Who & What is the Abomination of Desolation

precepts.why: What are the rivers she passes over? “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. The water is represented by the word; the word is represented as water.

note.label: Flawed Apologetic Doctrine

precepts.why: When did he come to us by water? “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. The washing of water is by the word.

note.label: The Getaway 3

precepts.why: “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness”: not some fellowship, not a little pocket of sin left open. Those works can come by family, friends, your job, the social media avenues. “But rather reprove them”: some of you got to cut off your friends who still bring up worldly conversation, cut off family members who are wicked as hell, and limit the time you talk to co-workers whose conversation leads you to porn, fornication and adultery. This scripture doesn’t change person to person; there’s no magical Shazam Marvel superhero scripture. The Most High wants you to fight; every moment you have the breath of life, that’s the grace under Christ to get it right. How long you going to be fighting with youthful lust, that chronic masturbator, chronic foot fetish, chronic crossdresser? We got to get it together.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
Christ is that water. Now we are purified with the water of Christ, which is the word: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

This is what the Pharisees stumbled on: they could not understand that Christ replaced all those things; they were a shadow of things to come. “That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.”

note.label: Living Martyrs

precepts.why:
Weigh it with this: “For scarcely for a righteous man will one die.” Scarcely, meaning you have to think about it. Am I really willing to sacrifice myself for this brother, much less a big mouth, loud mouth pterodactyl wife? Some men in the world die for that big mouth woman.

Even if it is a righteous brother, you have to think: am I willing to die for this brother, what does he really add to this truth? Some brothers have been here for years and add nothing; when you see their name or they come into the room, it is always problems. Am I really going to sacrifice myself for this dude?

“Yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die.” You might dare to die for a good man, somebody you know keeps the commandments, and give your life for him.

note.label: Living Martyrs

precepts.why:
This is the average black man: “many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes. Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.” Many have died for women, and it is all in a negative context.

Men have to get their minds right. Never sacrifice your life for a loud, evil, big mouth, disrespectful black woman. If she is getting beat up on the street and you decide to intervene, now you are dead too. A lot of our sisters instigate problems out in the world; they summon Satan, then Satan comes back on them and they want you to help. Like the woman who hit herself with a brick and said black men beat her up, and ran one scam after another; or the woman who busts her head on the sink and calls 911 and says he hit me; or the woman with a doctorate who ordered a refrigerator that wouldn’t fit, wouldn’t pay to send it back, and attacked the two delivery men. A woman that has never been disciplined, never been corrected: you don’t lay down your life for that.

note.label: Living Martyrs

precepts.why: Here is the answer: “Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.” That is the love the Lord is looking for: that a man lay down his life for his friends. And in order to have friends, you have to show yourself friendly. Some of you are not friendly.

note.label: THE REWARD OF THE RIGHTEOUS: WHO IS REALLY GETTING IN?

precepts.why:
“Their spot is not the spot of his children.” Christ is to “present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.” That is how we are supposed to be: presented as a glorious church, holy, without spot or blemish.

Instead we are so spotted up. That is why Moses said our spot is not the spot of his children: we are not following Christ and not matching what Christ is doing.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them”: have no friendship with them. Christ was among the indiscreet, but he wasn’t shooting the breeze with them; he was reproving them with the scriptures to win them to the truth. Don’t compare yourself to Christ when you’re sitting down smoking with the local drug dealer.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
These are the type of folks you need to cut off. “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness”: fellowship means friendship. Y’all going to the bar together, hanging out at each other’s house: have no fellowship. “But rather reprove them”: rather correct them.

“For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret.” Some of the vile filth they do in secret: threesomes and foursomes, wife swapping.
